chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ali ibn Maysara, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The husband is more rightful with his wife until he places her in her grave.
ai.seo_question: What is the husband's legal right over his wife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the scope of *wilayah* (guardianship) within the marital bond, emphasizing that the husband’s right of custody persists through the transition of death until the wife is laid to rest. This principle underscores the continuity of spousal rights in Shia jurisprudence, linking the legal status of the wife during life to the physical care and burial rites performed by the husband. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the practical implications of marital authority in both legal and ritual contexts.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Ali Bin Maysara, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The husband is more rightful with his wife until he places her in her grave’.
en.sarwar: 6. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from Ali ibn Maysarah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
a husband is more rightful to place his wife in the grave.”
